steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The hoplite phalanx was the dominant Greek fighting formation: a dense line of heavily armed infantry fighting shoulder to shoulder | Key Fact: Each hoplite carried an aspis (large round shield), dory (long spear), Corinthian helmet, bronze cuirass and greaves | Key Fact: The phalanx's strength lay in solidarity: each man's shield protected his neighbour's right side, creating an interdependent wall | Key Fact: Naval warfare became crucial after the Persian Wars; the trireme (three-banked oared warship) was the standard warship

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from greek warfare &amp; the hoplite phalanx, and one past-paper question.
